transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

The issue is likely that the sensor isn't detecting the water level correctly rather than the tank actually being full. This often happens if the container isn't pushed all the way home or if a small plastic float inside it gets stuck with limescale or fluff. Please slide the container out, check that the internal float moves freely up and down, and then reinsert it firmly until it clicks into place. Let me know if this resolves the error.
Yes I've re-seated it firmly, it clicks in. I cleaned the little filter/sieve in the container too, it was slimy. Still stops with the light on, any other ideas?

[Heading: Likely cause: float switch]
Since the container is most likely empty but the light stays on, the sensor that detects the water level (the float switch or electronic sensor) is likely failing to register that it's clear. To identify the correct replacement part for your specific Bosch model, I need the full model number from the rating plate inside the door opening.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

I only know it starts WTG8 from the front of the manual. The full label is on the back and the dryer is stacked on the washer so I can't get at it or move it. Is there anything else I can check from the front?

[Heading: Likely cause: float switch]
This points to a failure in the appliance's detection system rather than an actual water issue. On Bosch heat-pump dryers, there is often a small float switch inside the bottom sump (the reservoir at the base of the machine) that tells the electronics when the tank is full; if this gets stuck with limescale or sludge, it will falsely trigger the light even if the tank is empty. Because your model label is unreachable and the internal components require dismantling to access and clean safely, I recommend contacting Bosch Customer Support or a qualified engineer. They can diagnose whether the float switch needs cleaning or replacing, or if there is an issue with the electronic control board.

claimsRejected.claim: emptying the tank hasn't cleared the light

candidates: Water container not seated correctly or faulty float switch in the tank (high)
Clogged condenser causing poor drainage and sensor confusion (medium)
Faulty condensate pump or internal blockage (low)
